title: Security Advisory for PHP packages hosted at packagist.org
description: Security Advisory for PHP packages hosted at packagist.org on GitHub

items.content_html:
Magento versions 2.4.9-alpha2, 2.4.8-p2, 2.4.7-p7, 2.4.6-p12, 2.4.5-p14, 2.4.4-p15 and earlier are affected by an Incorrect Authorization vulnerability. A low-privileged attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized access to elevated privileges that increase integrity impact to high. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction.

References

  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-54267
  • https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/magento/apsb25-94.html
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvwr-p3hj-j6jf
items.title: [magento/community-edition] Magento vulnerable to privilege escalation due to incorrect authorization

items.content_html:
Refunds in general can be enabled through the administration setting core.cart.enableOrderRefunds (in the cart panel).Which visually shows and hides the button. However, using a custom crafted request, a customer can still cancel his own orders.As this is not checked inside the route (and also not in the controller): https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/trunk/src/Storefront/Controller/AccountOrderController.php#L98 https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/trunk/src/Core/Checkout/Order/SalesChannel/CancelOrderRoute.php

To mitigate this, a check should be added to the CancelOrderRoute which verifies that the feature is enabled.

References

  • https://github.com/shopware/shopware/security/advisories/GHSA-r2vg-hvjm-fg38
  • https://github.com/shopware/shopware/commit/b157508aef2c820e7ff89ebd5848d3019f22b592
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r2vg-hvjm-fg38
items.title: [shopware/core] Shopware Customer Orders can be canceled, even if refunds are disabled
